archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (possession rebound)
archetype.definition: A former champion whose 5-on-5 control has bounced back to near its Cup-era levels, but whose cold finishing and leaky special teams have kept the record and goal differential middling so far.

report.headline: The puck is back on Florida's sticks; the goals and the penalty kill haven't followed.
report.take:
Florida spent four seasons as one of the league's elite teams, with two 16-win playoff runs. Then came last year's 40-38-4 slide to 23rd on the site, with a sub-50 xGF % and goaltending that cost it goals. Seven games into 2026-27, the record is an unremarkable 3-2-2 and the Goal Diff / GP sits 20th at -0.14. Underneath that, this looks a lot more like the old Panthers than last year's version.

The main signal is territory. Florida owns 55% of 5-on-5 shot attempts, fifth in the league and right in line with its Cup years, and 53% of the expected goals. The depth is driving it. Anton Lundell, Eetu Luostarinen and Sandis Vilmanis are all above 62% xGF, and Lundell has 20 shots for one goal. Jacob Markstrom has been worth 2.6 goals above expected, so this isn't a team getting bailed out. It's out-chancing opponents and not converting: a 98.8 PDO, the 23rd-ranked offense and 2.71 goals a game, with nearly half of the 19 goals bunched into a 7-3 win in Columbus.

The numbers also hide some real problems. The PK is 23rd at 75.9%, and that is where a possession team bleeds the games it controls. The top line's results don't match its usage. Sam Reinhart has 4 goals but a 33.4% xGF in 21 minutes a night, and Brady Tkachuk is -5 with a 44.2% share, so the stars' production is coming more from the power play than from driving play. Matthew Tkachuk has carried the offense with 10 points and ranks fifth on the wingers' tab. Seth Jones, logging nearly 26 minutes, is the 10th-ranked defenseman.

The schedule also flattered no one. All but one game so far came on the road, including a West Coast swing. With a soft-looking homestand next and a roster grading B+/B/A-, the expectation is that the goals catch up to the chances. That makes Florida a playoff-caliber team that will look better in a month than it does now.

strengths.title: Cup-era possession has returned
strengths.body: Florida's 55% Corsi ranks fifth, and its 53% xGF is a clear jump from last season's 49.3%. The process is being driven by the middle-six forwards, which is more durable than a top line on a heater. Possession is the stickiest team stat early in a season, so this should mostly hold.

strengths.title: Markstrom has stabilized the crease
strengths.body: Last year's goalies were 8.8 goals below expected. This year Markstrom is +2.6 GSAx with a 2.03 GAA and a shutout, ranking ninth on the goalies' tab, and the team grades A- in goal. His .904 save % says he's solid rather than unconscious, which makes the gain believable.

strengths.title: Matthew Tkachuk and Jones driving offense
strengths.body: Tkachuk's 10 points lead the team and rank him fifth among wingers. Jones has 7 points from the back end in heavy minutes. Together they're the engine of a power play that has produced much of the scoring.

concerns.title: Finishing hasn't matched the chances
concerns.body: Florida ranks 23rd in goals per game while ranking top-five in shot share. A 98.8 PDO points to cold shooting rather than a broken offense. Bennett has no goals on 11 shots and Lundell has one on 20. This is the most likely thing to fix itself.

concerns.title: A penalty kill giving games away
concerns.body: The 75.9% PK ranks 23rd. That's well below the 81% it managed even in last year's down season, and it matches the 2022-23 rate. Seven games is a tiny special-teams sample, but this is the leak most capable of wasting a possession edge.

concerns.title: Top-line minutes, bottom-line shares
concerns.body: Reinhart's 33.4% xGF in 21 minutes a game is the worst on the roster. Brady Tkachuk is at 44.2% and -5. Their goals are coming largely on the power play, and if the 5-on-5 trend holds, the top of the lineup will be a drag at even strength.

trend.note: Florida has not won consecutive games yet, alternating results through a road-heavy opening. The underlying play has been consistently good, and the 7-3 win in Columbus was the first sign of the finishing catching up.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games, three opponents getting outshot badly
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with Florida's second and third home games of the season, against Vancouver and Seattle. The Canucks are 29th on the site, with the league's worst penalty kill and goaltending 8.7 goals below expected. That's an ideal setting for a cold offense to break out. Seattle is 5-2-0 and eighth on the site, but it's riding a 108.3 PDO while owning only 42% of shot attempts. Florida's possession game is exactly what exposes that kind of team.

The road back-to-back at Ottawa and Pittsburgh is tougher. The Senators are 5-2-0 but third in Pts vs Goal Diff and get outshot too. Pittsburgh is the one opponent with a real 5-on-5 game, a 54% xGF share, plus an A- blueline and a 89.5% kill that could stall Florida's power play. Against two outshot opponents and a soft Vancouver, five or more points from the four games is a reasonable target.

keyMatchups.title: Cold offense versus Vancouver's leaky kill
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver kills 57.1% of penalties, 32nd in the league, and gives forwards more points than all but two teams. Florida's power-play-heavy top unit should feast here. If it can't, the scoring concern becomes more real.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle's hot start meets possession
keyMatchups.body: The Kraken rank third in offense but 30th in shot share, with a 108.3 PDO. Florida's fifth-ranked Corsi tests whether Seattle's shooting and goaltending can keep outrunning the shot counts. Seattle is stingy against defensemen, so expect Florida's scoring to have to come from the forwards.

keyMatchups.title: Pittsburgh's wingers hole, back-to-back goalie
keyMatchups.body: The Penguins give wingers 0.97 points a game over expected, 28th in the league. That's an opening for Matthew Tkachuk. The second game of a back-to-back may bring Akira Schmid, whose .875 save % is a real drop from Markstrom's.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Florida's even-strength shooting finally converts on the homestand. Goals from Lundell, Bennett and the depth lines would turn the possession edge into wins.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts of Florida's game that tend to persist look healthy: a top-five shot share, a 53% expected-goal share and a starter saving more than expected. The parts dragging the record down are the noisy ones, namely a sub-100 PDO, cold depth shooting and seven games of penalty-kill results. Expect the goal differential to move positive and the offense to climb from the bottom third toward the middle of the league. The Pts vs Goal Diff edge is small enough not to matter either way.

The caveats are real, though. The top line's poor 5-on-5 shares could turn this into a team that controls the puck with its depth but loses the minutes that matter most. Markstrom has to keep carrying the bulk of the starts, given how Schmid has looked. In a crowded Atlantic, this projects as a playoff team rather than a contender. It should be a clear step up from last year's 84-point finish.
swingFactors: Penalty kill returning to the 80% range
Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk at even strength

confidence.note: Seven games, almost all on the road; possession signals are encouraging but samples are tiny.
